```{r}
#| include: false

# Set path to variable: Tropical_Cyclones
# This is where the data are and where the plots will go
Dir <- here("Tropical_Cyclones")
# Check if it exists; if not, create it
if (!dir.exists(Dir)) {
  dir.create(Dir)
}
```

```{r}
#| include: false
### Load data
# Read in a saved csv file with manual edits following the notes at the bottom of this script.
#ibtracs_full <- read_csv(file = paste(Dir, '/ibtracs.since1980.list.v04r01_', RptYr, '.csv', sep = ""))
#ibtracs_full <- readRDS(paste0(Dir, '/ibtracesTemp.rds'))

# Because the URL changes every year I'm trying to automate it below
# It's a very large file so it takes a while to read it in.
# 1Base URL for IBTrACS dataset directory
base_url <- "https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/data/international-best-track-archive-for-climate-stewardship-ibtracs/"

# Read the root HTML directory and find version subfolders (e.g., v04r01, v04r00)
root_html <- read_html(base_url)

version_folders <- root_html %>%
  html_nodes("a") %>%
  html_attr("href") %>%
  grep("^v[0-9]+", ., value = TRUE) %>%  # Filter for version patterns (e.g., v04r01/)
  sort(decreasing = TRUE)               # Sort to get the latest version first

if (length(version_folders) == 0) {
  stop("Could not find any version folders at the specified URL.")
}

latest_version_folder <- version_folders[1]

# Construct the URL for the CSV subfolder
csv_dir_url <- paste0(base_url, latest_version_folder, "/access/csv/")

# Read the CSV directory and find the file containing "since1980" in its filename
csv_dir_html <- read_html(csv_dir_url)

csv_files <- csv_dir_html %>%
  html_nodes("a") %>%
  html_attr("href") %>%
  grep("since1980.*\\.csv$", ., value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)

target_file_name <- csv_files[1]
target_file_url <- paste0(csv_dir_url, target_file_name)

# Read the CSV file into an R data frame
# Note: IBTrACS CSVs include header row metadata/units in row 2
# Peek at the top 2 rows to retrieve original column names and units
header_preview <- vroom(target_file_url, n_max = 2, col_names = FALSE, show_col_types = FALSE)
# Pull out the header information
names_row <- unlist(header_preview[1, ])
units_row <- unlist(header_preview[2, ])

# The data has a lot of columns so here define the target columns we want to load
keep_cols <- c("SID", "SEASON", "NUMBER", "BASIN", "SUBBASIN", "ISO_TIME", "LAT", "LON", "WMO_WIND", "USA_WIND", "USA_SSHS")

# Read ONLY those columns, skipping the top 2 rows
ibtracs_full <- vroom(
  target_file_url,
  skip = 2,
  col_names = names_row,                           # Assign base column names
  col_select = all_of(keep_cols),                 # Load only selected columns
  #na = c("", "NA", "-999", "-999.0", "NOT_NAMED") # Handle common IBTrACS NAs
)

# Append unit names to the retained columns
selected_units <- units_row[match(keep_cols, names_row)]
final_names <- ifelse(
  is.na(selected_units) | selected_units %in% c("", " ", "1"),
  keep_cols,
  paste(keep_cols, selected_units, sep = "_")
)
names(ibtracs_full) <- final_names

```

```{r}
#| include: false
### Handle the dates and times
ibtracs_full <- ibtracs_full %>% 
  rename(DATE_TIME = ISO_TIME)
#   #mutate(DATE_TIME = mdy_hm(ISO_TIME))

# We only want 6-hourly observations, as these are used in calculating ACE and other indicators
# We only want tropical cyclones (tropical depressions - cat 5)
ibtracs_6hrly <- ibtracs_full %>% 
  filter(hour(DATE_TIME) %in% seq(0,18,by=6) & USA_SSHS >= -1)

```

```{r}
#| include: false
### Add a category that groups storms into TD, TC, Cat 1 & 2, Major (Cat 3+) 
STORM_BIN <- case_match(ibtracs_6hrly$USA_SSHS, 
                        c(-1) ~ 1, # Tropical depression
                        c(0) ~ 2,  # Tropical storm
                        c(1, 2) ~ 3,  # Cat 1 & 2 storm2
                        c(3, 4, 5) ~ 4)  # Cat 3+ storms = major
ibtracs_6hrly <- bind_cols(ibtracs_6hrly, STORM_BIN = STORM_BIN)
#ibtracs_6hrly <- rename(ibtracs_6hrly, STORM_BIN = ...13)
```

```{r}
#| include: false
# Define by basin and subbasin
ibtracs_6hrly_basin <- ibtracs_6hrly %>%
  mutate(
    BASIN_tracs = case_when(
      BASIN == 'EP' & SUBBASIN != 'CP' ~ 'EP',
      BASIN == 'EP' & SUBBASIN == 'CP' ~ 'CP',
      BASIN == 'WP'                    ~ 'WP',
      BASIN == 'SP'                    ~ 'SP',
      TRUE                             ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(BASIN_tracs))
```

```{r}
#| include: false
# For ear year in each basin, we need to:
# -Identify unique storms of each category for that year
# -Sum the number of each
# -Determine the accumulated cyclone energy (ACE) for that basin and year
All_counts <- ibtracs_6hrly_basin %>%
  filter(SEASON_Year >= 1980, SEASON_Year <= RptYr) %>%
  group_by(Basin = BASIN_tracs, Year = SEASON_Year) %>%
  summarise(
    # Storm presence indicators (evaluates to TRUE/FALSE per storm, then summed)
    NumberNamed    = n_distinct(NUMBER[STORM_BIN == 2]),
    NumberCyclones = n_distinct(NUMBER[STORM_BIN == 3]),
    NumberMajor    = n_distinct(NUMBER[STORM_BIN == 4]),
    
    # ACE sum: sum(USA_WIND_kts^2)
    ACE = sum(USA_WIND_kts^2, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Complete missing years/basins with zeros if a basin had 0 storms in a given year
  complete(
    Basin = c("EP", "CP", "WP", "SP"),
    Year = 1980:RptYr,
    fill = list(NumberNamed = 0, NumberCyclones = 0, NumberMajor = 0, ACE = 0)
  )

# Isolate out just 2025 for each basin to easier populate the text
# We want any number <= 9 to be spelled out as we are using these in text below
# Function to convert numbers <= 9 to words, and keep >= 9 as numbers (or characters)
format_counts <- function(x) {
  ifelse(x <= 9, numbers_to_words(x), as.character(x))
}
# Apply conversion to count metrics
All_counts_text <- All_counts %>%
  mutate(across(c(NumberNamed, NumberCyclones, NumberMajor), format_counts))
# Isolate out the reporting year for each basin
EP_yr <- All_counts_text %>% filter(Year == RptYr, Basin == 'EP')
CP_yr <- All_counts_text %>% filter(Year == RptYr, Basin == 'CP')
WP_yr <- All_counts_text %>% filter(Year == RptYr, Basin == 'WP')
SP_yr <- All_counts_text %>% filter(Year == RptYr, Basin == 'SP')

# We also need to average these over the 1991 - 2020 period
All_avg <- All_counts %>% 
  filter(Year >= 1991 & Year <= 2020) %>% 
  group_by(Basin) %>% 
  summarise_all(mean, na.rm=T) %>% 
  select(!Year)

```

```{r}
#| include: false
# And, now, a bunch of linear models to look for trends in storm counts or ACE
# only p-values < 0.05 are noted
# Named storms
All_lm <- All_counts %>%
  mutate(Total = rowSums(across(NumberNamed:NumberMajor), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = NumberNamed:Total, ) %>%
  group_by(Basin, name) %>% 
  nest() %>% 
  mutate(model = map(data, ~lm(value ~ Year, data = .x)), 
         results = map(model, tidy)) %>% 
  unnest(results)
  
All_lm %>% 
  filter(term == 'Year', p.value < 0.05) #%>% 
  #select(Basin, name) %>% ungroup()

```

```{r}
#| include: false
### Create plot for report
# Palette for storm map - Follows NOAA standards
# TD_col <- '#929292'
# TS_col <- '#606060'
# Cat1_col <- '#ffdc00'
# Cat2_col <- '#ff9e00'
# Cat3_col <- '#ff2600'
# Cat4_col <- '#942192'    
# Cat5_col <- '#ff40ff'
land_col <- '#cbb397'
coast_col <- '#888583'
ocean_col <- '#97b6e1'
map_pal <- scale_color_manual(values = c('-1' = '#929292',
                                         '0' = '#606060', 
                                         '1' = '#ffdc00', 
                                         '2' = '#ff9e00', 
                                         '3' = '#ff2600', 
                                         '4' = '#942192', 
                                         '5' = '#ff40ff'), 
                              labels = c('Tropical Depression', 
                                         'Tropical Storm', 
                                         'Category 1', 
                                         'Category 2', 
                                         'Category 3', 
                                         'Category 4', 
                                         'Category 5'), 
                              name=NULL)

# Isolate the report year and fix lons to 0-360
tracks2025 <- ibtracs_6hrly_basin %>% 
  filter(SEASON_Year == RptYr) %>% 
  mutate(LON_degrees_east = (LON_degrees_east + 360) %% 360)

# Get rid of duplicate numbers for two basins
#tracks2025$NUMBER[which(tracks2025$NUMBER == 104 & tracks2025$BASIN == 'SP')] <- max(tracks2025$NUMBER)+10

# Access map base data (using the shapefile from maps world2 becuase it's already dealt with the dateline)
land_proj_tc <- st_as_sf(maps::map('world2', xlim=c(90,280), ylim=c(-48,48), plot = FALSE, fill = TRUE))
ext <- c(90, -48, 280, 48)

p <- ggplot() +
        geom_sf(data = land_proj_tc, fill = land_col, color = coast_col, linewidth = 0.2) +
        coord_sf(xlim = c(ext[1], ext[3]), ylim = c(ext[2], ext[4]), expand = F) +
        geom_path(data=tracks2025, aes(LON_degrees_east, LAT_degrees_north, group = NUMBER, colour = as.character(USA_SSHS))) + 
        map_pal +
        theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = ocean_col),
              panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth=0.1, colour = '#d2e0f2'),
              panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
              axis.text = element_text(size=12),
              legend.position = 'inside',
              legend.justification.inside = c(1, 0),
              legend.background = element_rect(fill = 'gray90', color='transparent'),
              legend.text = element_text(size=12),
              legend.key = element_blank(),
              legend.key.spacing.y = unit(-0.13,'cm')) +
        scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(120, 180, 240)) +
        scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(-40,40,by=20)) +
        xlab(NULL) + ylab(NULL)
  
#ggsave(filename = paste0(Dir, '/TC_map_', RptYr, '.pdf'), plot = p, width=7.8, height=4, units='in')
```

```{r}
#| include: false

# Define the color palette
NS_col  <- rgb(149, 196, 223, maxColorValue = 255)
HTC_col <- rgb(46, 126, 188, maxColorValue = 255)
MAJ_col <- rgb(8, 48, 107, maxColorValue = 255)

# Axis scaling factor: maps ACE (0-700) onto Storm Count axis (0-40)
# If plotting in ggplot you have to scale the secondary y-axis to the primary y-axis, it doesn't allow for an independent secondary y-axis. 
scale_factor <- 40 / 700
#full_years   <- 1980:RptYr

# Prepare single unified dataset for all basins
plot_data <- All_counts %>%
  # Join baseline averages for horizontal baseline
  left_join(All_avg %>% select(Basin, ACE_avg = ACE), by = "Basin") %>%
  # Pivot counts long for category fills
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(NumberNamed, NumberCyclones, NumberMajor),
    names_to = "Category",
    values_to = "Count"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Set facet ordering and clean basin titles
    Basin = factor(
      Basin,
      levels = c("EP", "CP", "WP", "SP"),
      labels = c("Eastern Pacific (EP)", "Central Pacific (CP)", "Western Pacific (WP)", "South Pacific (SP)")
    ),
    # Set legend category labels
    Category = factor(
      Category,
      levels = c("NumberNamed", "NumberCyclones", "NumberMajor"),
      labels = c(
        "Named Storms",
        "Hurricanes (EP & CP), Typhoons (WP), Cyclones (SP)",
        "Major Hurricanes (EP & CP), Typhoons (WP), Cyclones (SP)"
      )
    )
  )

# Make a plot using facets for each basin
TCcounts <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Year)) +
  # Grouped Bar Plot for Storm Counts
  geom_col(aes(y = Count, fill = Category), position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  # Annual ACE Line
  geom_line(aes(y = (ACE / 1e4) * scale_factor, color = "Annual ACE Index"), linewidth = 0.6) +
  # 1991-2020 Average ACE Line
  geom_line(aes(y = (ACE_avg / 1e4) * scale_factor, color = "1991-2020 average ACE Index"), linewidth = 0.6) +
  # Facet into 4 vertically stacked panels
  facet_wrap(~ Basin, ncol = 1, scales = 'free_x') +
  # Manual Fill and Color Scales
  scale_fill_manual(name = "Category", values = c(NS_col, HTC_col, MAJ_col)) +
  scale_color_manual(name = "Metric", values = c("Annual ACE Index" = "#646464", "1991-2020 average ACE Index" = "#D0D0D0")) +
  # Dual Y-Axes with Global Titles
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Storm Count", limits = c(0, 40), sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / scale_factor, name = expression(bold(paste("Accumulated Cyclone Energy (ACE) Index (10"^4, " kts"^2, ")")))), expand = F) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1980, RptYr, by = 5), expand = c(0.005,0.005)) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    # Facet Header Strip Styling
    strip.background = element_blank(), #element_rect(fill = "gray90", color = "gray50"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    # Axis Titles & Grid Lines
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    axis.title.y.right = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    # Bottom Legend with 2 Columns
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.box = "horizontal",
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9), 
    # Plot panel box
    panel.border = element_blank(), 
    axis.line.y = element_line(color='black', linewidth = 0.6),
    # Increasing font size on the axis numbers
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12, color = "black"),
    axis.text.y.right = element_text(size = 12, color = "black"),
    # Increase X-axis tick mark numbers
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, color = "black")
  ) +
  guides(
    fill  = guide_legend(ncol = 1, order = 1),  # Column 1: Categories
    color = guide_legend(ncol = 1, order = 2, override.aes = list(linewidth = 1.2))   # Column 2: ACE Metrics
  )

#ggsave(filename = paste0(Dir, '/TC_counts_', RptYr, '.pdf'), plot = p, width=8, height=8, units='in')
```

**Rationale:** The effects of tropical cyclones are numerous and well known. At sea, storms disrupt and endanger shipping traffic as well as fishing effort and safety. The Hawaiʻi longline fishery, for example, has had serious problems with vessels dodging storms at sea, delayed departures, and inability to make it safely back to Honolulu because of bad weather. When cyclones encounter land, their intense rains and high winds can cause severe property damage, loss of life, soil erosion, and flooding. Associated storm surge, the large volume of ocean water pushed toward shore by cyclones’ strong winds, can cause severe flooding and destruction.

**Status:**
*Eastern North Pacific.* Tropical cyclone activity was above average in the Eastern Pacific in `r RptYr`. There were `r EP_yr$NumberNamed` named storms, `r EP_yr$NumberCyclones` of which were hurricanes. There were `r EP_yr$NumberMajor` major hurricanes (category 3 or higher). Accumulated Cyclone Energy (ACE) was near average at about `r round(EP_yr$ACE/All_avg$ACE[which(All_avg$Basin == 'EP')]*100,-1)`% the 1991–2020 average in the Eastern North Pacific.  <!--In addition to season totals, early season tropical cyclone activity and ACE were at a record low in 2024, with this being only the second year in this time series with no activity in June. -->
Portions of this summary inserted from <https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/monitoring/monthly-report/tropical-cyclones/202506> and <https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/monitoring/monthly-report/tropical-cyclones/202507>.  

*Central North Pacific.*  <!-- Early season tropical cyclone activity and ACE were at a record low in 2024 in the Central North Pacific. with this being only the second year in this time series with no activity in June. On August 19th, Hurricane Hone formed in the Central Pacific and peaked as a Category 1 hurricane with winds of 85 mph and a minimum central pressure of 988 mb. Hone brought gusty winds and flooding rains to the Island of Hawaiʻi as it passed south of the island chain. Overall,--> Central Pacific tropical cyclone activity was slightly above the 1991–2020 average in `r RptYr`. There were `r CP_yr$NumberNamed` named storms, `r CP_yr$NumberCyclones` hurricanes, and `r CP_yr$NumberMajor` major hurricanes. On average (1991–2020), the central Pacific sees four named storms, two hurricanes, and one major hurricane each year.  The `r RptYr` ACE index was near the 1991–2020 average. Portions of this summary inserted from  <https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/monitoring/monthly-report/tropical-cyclones/202506>, <https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/monitoring/monthly-report/tropical-cyclones/202507>, <https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/monitoring/monthly-report/tropical-cyclones/202508>.

*Western North Pacific.* Early season tropical cyclone activity and ACE were below average in `r RptYr`. <!--The last four named storms of November were at one point all simultaneously active, becoming the first instance of four simultaneous named storms in the West Pacific during the month of November. Overall, due to the extremely high activity the ACE value in the West Pacific was over 200% of average for the month.-->  The Western Pacific saw `r WP_yr$NumberNamed` named storms in `r RptYr`.  Of these storms, `r WP_yr$NumberCyclones` were typhoons, and `r WP_yr$NumberMajor` became major typhoons. These counts were all close to average (1991–2020), although ACE was only about `r round(WP_yr$ACE/All_avg$ACE[which(All_avg$Basin == 'WP')]*100,-1)`% the long-term average.  Since 1980, the number of named storms and typhoons has decreased slightly at a rate of about one storm per decade and the number of total storms has decreased at a rate of about two storms per decade.  Portions of the summary inserted from  <https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/monitoring/monthly-report/tropical-cyclones/202506>, <https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/monitoring/monthly-report/tropical-cyclones/202507>, <https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/monitoring/monthly-report/tropical-cyclones/202508>.  

*South Pacific.* South Pacific tropical cyclone activity was slightly below average in `r RptYr`.  There were `r SP_yr$NumberNamed` named storms, `r SP_yr$NumberCyclones` of which became cyclones and `r SP_yr$NumberMajor`  major cyclones.  The `r RptYr` ACE was `r round(SP_yr$ACE/All_avg$ACE[which(All_avg$Basin == 'SP')]*100)`% of the 1991–2020 average.  

**Description:** This indicator uses historical data from the NOAA National Climate Data Center (NCDC) International Best Track Archive for Climate Stewardship to track the number of tropical cyclones in the western, central, eastern, and southern Pacific basins. This indicator also monitors the Accumulated Cyclone Energy (ACE) Index and the Power Dissipation Index which are two ways of monitoring the frequency, strength, and duration of tropical cyclones based on wind speed measurements.

The annual frequency of storms passing through each basin is tracked and @fig-ch6-TCcount shows the representative breakdown of Saffir-Simpson hurricane categories.  

Every cyclone has an ACE Index value, which is a number based on the maximum wind speed measured at six-hourly intervals over the entire time that the cyclone is classified as at least a tropical storm (wind speed of at least 34 knots; 39 mph). Therefore, a storm’s ACE Index value accounts for both strength and duration. @fig-ch6-TCcount shows the ACE values for each hurricane/typhoon season and has a horizontal line representing the average annual ACE value.  

*Note: Plotted on the map are only storms classified as Tropical Disturbances or stronger*

**Timeframe:** Annual.  

**Region/Location:** 
	Eastern North Pacific: east of 140° W, north of the equator.
	
	Central North Pacific: 180° - 140° W, north of the equator.
	
	Western North Pacific: west of 180°, north of the equator.
	
	South Pacific: south of the equator.
	
**Measurement Platform:** Satellite.  

**Data available at:** <https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/data/international-best-track-archive-for-climate-stewardship-ibtracs/v04r01/access/csv/>.  

**Sourced from:** @Knapp2010-rc and @Gahtan2024-dr.
